subject.title: Exec allowlist matches never auto-execute on darwin — "allowlist auto-execution is unavailable on darwin; reviewer or explicit approval is required" (2026.6.11)

question: Should Darwin gateway allowlist matches that require shell expansion or wrapper syntax auto-execute after a successful allowlist match, or remain prompt-only with clearer docs and diagnostics?
rationale: Current code requires an enforceable command reconstruction before auto-executing matched allowlist commands; relaxing that requirement changes what OpenClaw treats as safe unattended execution.

options.title: Support a narrow safe subset
options.body: Allow only well-defined Darwin-safe shapes such as tilde expansion or independently allowlisted simple chains, with focused tests and live macOS proof.

options.title: Keep prompt-only and document it
options.body: Preserve the current security posture while updating docs and warning text so operators can convert automation to argv-clean absolute-path commands.

options.title: Defer to broader exec authorization design
options.body: Leave the issue open but block runtime changes until maintainers settle a cross-platform shell authorization model.

recommendation.title: Support a narrow safe subset
recommendation.body: Allow only well-defined Darwin-safe shapes such as tilde expansion or independently allowlisted simple chains, with focused tests and live macOS proof.
